title: Teaching
text: I teach statistics at every level at WPI, from the first applied statistics course to the graduate course in statistical genetics. My aim is understanding that lasts beyond the exam. For the courses I have redesigned I built topic-based materials, with lecture notes, recorded lectures, R examples and practice problems, and I share them with the colleagues who teach these courses.

Statistical Methods in Genetics and Bioinformatics is a course I created as the foundational statistics course of the Bioinformatics and Computational Biology (BCB) degrees. It was taught as one cross-listed course until 2024, when growing enrollment led to separate undergraduate and graduate versions. The graduate version now runs as a semester-long course with a research-oriented class project, and it integrates AI-assisted learning into the coursework.

Structured AI Tutoring for Applied Statistics: an AI-assisted practice tool for MA 2611, a course that serves more than 700 students a year. The tool delivers curated problems with adaptive difficulty and AI-generated feedback aligned to the course, through instructor-guided prompts and instructor-curated content rather than unstructured chatbot use.

title: Teaching
text:
Student projects
Students work with me on research projects at every level: PhD dissertations, master’s theses and capstone projects, undergraduate Major Qualifying Projects (MQPs) and Interactive Qualifying Projects (IQPs), and independent studies. So far I have advised 5 PhD dissertations, 7 master’s theses, 19 master’s capstone and research projects, 8 MQPs and 1 IQP, and 73 independent-study and project courses. The People page lists the projects.
Typical topics are statistical genetics and bioinformatics; statistical theory and methodology for signal detection, decision-making, prediction and causal inference; computational statistics, including the implementation of methods for large data and the development of R packages; and statistical applications in engineering, experimental design and business. Students are welcome to bring their own ideas that match the group’s interests.
What I expect. Research requires self-motivation, curiosity, patience and effort, and a dedication to excellent work that goes beyond earning the credits. A successful project usually takes 20 hours a week or more.
How a project runs. We meet weekly to discuss progress, challenges and next steps. Students submit weekly reports summarizing their methods and results, with the code organized on GitHub. Each project ends with a final report. For an outstanding project, I help prepare a manuscript for publication.
Undergraduates at WPI can read more about the MQP and the IQP. If you are interested in a project, email me with a short note on your background and what you would like to work on.

title: Zheyang Wu
text:
I am a Professor of Mathematical Sciences at Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI). I co-founded WPI’s Bioinformatics and Computational Biology program and teach its core statistics course, and I co-created the department’s PhD program in Statistics.
My research develops statistical methods for combining dependent evidence: p-value combination, signal detection, and integrative association testing. The methods are motivated by, and applied to, meta-analysis, whole-genome sequencing studies, statistical genetics, and clinical studies. My group releases the methods as open-source R packages.

title: Research
text: My research develops statistical methods for combining dependent evidence: p-value combination, signal detection and integrative association testing. The pieces of evidence to be combined, whether p-values from related tests, variants in a genomic region, or measurements from the same patients, are usually correlated. We study how to combine such evidence, how to compute the p-values of the combined tests accurately, and what the tests can detect, and we release the methods as R packages. The applications come from collaborations in genetics, neuroscience, biomechanics and clinical trials.

title: Research
text:
Topics

Combining dependent p-values
Fisher’s combination and its relatives are the workhorses of meta-analysis and of set-based association tests, but their null distributions under dependence are hard to compute. We developed p-value calculations for a general family of Fisher-type statistics under dependence (the GFisher family), truncation and weighting schemes for Fisher’s combination (TFisher), and adjustment and combination methods for discrete p-values, which arise from small-sample and exact tests. Recent work studies the correlation robustness of supremum-based p-value combination tests.

Hong Zhang and Zheyang Wu (2022). The Generalized Fisher’s Combination and Accurate p-Value Calculation under Dependence. Biometrics. doi:10.1111/biom.13634
Hong Zhang, Tiejun Tong, John E. Landers and Zheyang Wu (2020). TFisher: A powerful truncation and weighting procedure for combining p-values. Annals of Applied Statistics, 14(1): 178–201. doi:10.1214/19-AOAS1302
Gonzalo Contador and Zheyang Wu (2025). A minimum Wasserstein distance approach to Fisher’s combination of independent discrete p-values. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 52(3): 1281–1300. doi:10.1111/sjos.12787
Xiaohui Chen, Fangfang Wang, Hong Zhang and Zheyang Wu (2026). On Correlation Robustness of Supremum-based p-Value Combination Tests. Statistica Sinica, accepted. doi:10.5705/ss.202025.0263



Signal detection: theory and computation
When a few weak signals hide among many null features, the question is which statistics can detect them, and at what signal strength. We study detection boundaries and the finite-sample distributions of signal-detection statistics such as Higher Criticism and Berk-Jones, and we build approximations for the distributions that these and other tests need, including quadratic forms of Gaussian variables.

Zheyang Wu, Yiming Sun, Shiquan He, Judy Cho, Hongyu Zhao and Jiashun Jin (2014). Detection Boundary and Higher Criticism for Weak and Sparse Genetic Effects. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 8(2): 824–851. doi:10.1214/14-AOAS724
Hong Zhang, Jiashun Jin and Zheyang Wu (2020). Distributions and Power of Optimal Signal-Detection Statistics in Finite Case. IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing, 68: 1021–1033. link
Hong Zhang, Judong Shen and Zheyang Wu (2021). An efficient and accurate approximation to the distribution of quadratic forms of Gaussian variables. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics. doi:10.1080/10618600.2021.2000423
Zheyang Wu and Huibin Zhou (2013). Model Selection and Sharp Asymptotic Minimaxity. Probability Theory and Related Fields, 156(1-2): 165–191. doi:10.1007/s00440-012-0424-5



Integrative association testing for sequencing studies
Whole-genome sequencing studies test regions that hold many rare variants of small effect. Power depends on how the variants are weighted and how their evidence is integrated. We develop integrated weighted association tests and study the signal-to-noise ratio of genetic associations, and we apply this work in genetic studies of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and osteoporosis. The GLOW software below implements integrative variant-set association tests with optimized weights for whole-genome sequencing studies.

Hong Zhang, Ming Liu, John E. Landers and Zheyang Wu (2026). Integrated Weighted Association Test with Application to Genetic Association Studies. Annals of Applied Statistics, accepted.
Hong Zhang, Ming Liu, Jiashun Jin and Zheyang Wu (2023). Signal-noise ratio of genetic associations and statistical power of SNP-set tests. Annals of Applied Statistics, 17(3): 2410–2431. doi:10.1214/22-AOAS1725
Xiaohui Chen, Hong Zhang, Ming Liu, Hong-Wen Deng and Zheyang Wu (2022). Simultaneous detection of novel genes and SNPs by adaptive p-value combination. Frontiers in Genetics. doi:10.3389/fgene.2022.1009428
Bradley N. Smith et al. (2014). Exome-wide rare variant analysis identifies TUBA4A mutations associated with familial ALS. Neuron, 84(2): 324–331. doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2014.09.027



Clinical and biomedical studies
With clinicians and engineers we design and analyse studies where the statistical question is part of the science: augmenting clinical trial data with external controls, and an assumption-agnostic deep learning framework for trial monitoring; predicting outcomes from biomechanical models of atherosclerotic plaques and of the brain under impact; and predicting patient-reported pain from wearable sensors.

Shaoming Yin, Jianchang Lin and Zheyang Wu (2026). Augmenting clinical trial data with external controls through energy balancing weighted power prior. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research. doi:10.1080/19466315.2025.2587049
Shaoming Yin, Zheyang Wu and Jianchang Lin (2026). Assumption-agnostic deep learning framework for holistic clinical trial monitoring. Therapeutic Innovation & Regulatory Science, 60: 782–797. doi:10.1007/s43441-026-00915-1
David Clement, Emmanuel Agu, Atifa Sarwar, Deepak Kumar, Zheyang Wu and Jean A. King (2026). Machine learning Prediction of Self-Reported Real-World Knee Osteoarthritis Pain from Wearable Accelerometer-Derived Gait Features. Scientific Reports, accepted. doi:10.1038/s41598-026-64594-6
Nan Lin, Shaoju Wu, Zheyang Wu and Songbai Ji (2024). Efficient Generation of Pretraining Samples for Developing a Deep Learning Brain Injury Model via Transfer Learning. Annals of Biomedical Engineering, 52(10): 2726–2740. doi:10.1007/s10439-023-03354-3

title: Research
text:
Software
Research software is in the ZWuLab GitHub organization; the first five packages below are on CRAN.








Package
What it does
Where




GFisher
p-values for the general family of Fisher-type combination statistics (Fisher, Good, Lancaster) under dependence
CRAN · GitHub · docs


TFisher
optimal thresholding and weighting for Fisher’s p-value combination
CRAN · GitHub


DPComb
combination tests for discrete p-values
CRAN · GitHub


SetTest
group-testing procedures for signal detection and goodness of fit: Higher Criticism, Berk-Jones, one-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov and phi-divergence tests, with distributions, power and random numbers
CRAN · GitHub


Qapprox
tail probabilities of quadratic forms of Gaussian variables
CRAN · GitHub


GLOWr
integrative variant-set association analysis with optimized weights for whole-genome sequencing studies
GitHub · docs


GLOWpipeline
genome-wide GLOW scans: chunking, cluster job arrays, aggregation and locus merging
GitHub · docs


GLOWanalyses
runnable end-to-end workflow templates, configurations and batch scripts for sequencing studies
GitHub
